llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly retrieves the PPTX file and checks slide 0 for all three content areas: title (shape[0]), body (shape[1]), and table (shape[2]), matching the instruction 'all text including table content'.
Metric correctly awards partial credit (0.34 title + 0.33 body + 0.33 table = 1.0) aligned with the three coverage areas in the instruction.
Color comparison uses RGB tolerance of 15 against C00000 (dark red), which handles minor LibreOffice rounding differences correctly.
run.font.color.type is None check correctly rejects unset/inherited colors, requiring explicit RGB assignment.
Initial state (black/white text) will not pass the check, providing negative-control resistance.
Table cell traversal via row > cell > text_frame > paragraphs > runs is the correct python-pptx approach.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Shape indices are hardcoded (0=title, 1=body, 2=table); consider using shape.name or shape.placeholder_format to identify shapes robustly if the file structure is uncertain.

If LibreOffice saves table text color as a theme reference, run.font.color.rgb could return a computed rather than direct value; consider adding a fallback that also checks theme color RGB resolution.
